findings.claim: b64Closed reports an empty or one-character payload as closed, so a pane captured just after b64: was printed is refused, and the request is marked failed with no way to recover it.
findings.evidence: For 'b64:' or 'b64:e', Buffer.from(...,'base64') decodes to an empty string. The empty string does not start with a brace, so b64Closed returns true and decodeReviewPayload refuses it. collectReview then records the request as failed, and the new TM-220 check at line 723 refuses every later collect of that nonce.
findings.fix: In b64Closed, return false when the decoded text is empty or whitespace (or when the base64 is shorter than 4 characters), so a capture taken mid-print waits like an unclosed JSON prefix does. Add a test that captures 'AO_REVIEW <nonce> b64:' and expects RESPONSE_INCOMPLETE rather than a failed request.

findings.claim: The b64 rejoin loop appends any following indented row made only of base64-alphabet characters, so a single-word row printed after the verdict corrupts a complete payload.
findings.evidence: The loop condition only tests the next trimmed row against the base64 alphabet. It never stops once the payload has ended in padding or already decodes to closed JSON. A row such as '  Done' or '  OK' would be appended.
findings.fix: Stop appending once the payload ends in '=' or b64Closed(payload) is already true, or require each continuation row except the last to be as long as the preceding rows.

findings.claim: review publish still validates and publishes to the verdict subject, but collectReview no longer reads that subject on any transport, so a published verdict never reaches the merge gate. This matches the stated design (the pane is the only channel) but leaves review publish with no effect on collection.
The request includes no test-run output, so the new reviewer-findings tests and the changed orch-transport case are unverified. This approval rests on reading the diff, not on any check result.
